name: Coldbreak Oversized Hoodie — Port-Split Hood
description: Thick, boxy hoodie in charcoal with a kangaroo pocket and a hood split along one side seam to accommodate standard neural port clusters without bunching. Brushed interior, double-stitched cuffs. The kind of thing you wear to a bar in February and refuse to check at the door.
functionality: Port-split hood prevents neural port irritation; kangaroo pocket fits a full hand warmer and a flask.
what_it_says: You've got BCI and you're not hiding it, but you're not showing it off either.
story_hooks: The port-split design was originally filed by a the Gray Zone tailor who never got credit — the Circuit label just reverse-engineered it.
Someone's contact info is written inside the collar in permanent marker — still legible.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: Relaxed, streetwear silhouette with exaggerated box-cut shoulders and length that reaches mid-hip. The hood features an asymmetrical split seam along the right side, creating a deliberately open channel that frames rather than fully encloses the head—practical accommodation for visible neural port hardware. Reads as casual-tough, comfortable enough for a dive bar but intentionally designed for augmented bodies.
physical_description.fit: Oversized and boxy through the chest and torso, with dropped shoulders and generous sleeve length. Not tailored—deliberately slouchy, designed to drape over cybernetic augmentations without compression or binding. Cuffs are fitted with double-stitching for durability.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy brushed synth-wool blend, mid-grade thermal composite rated for GLMZ winters. Durable enough for repeated wear and machine wash, but not premium enough to signal wealth.
physical_description.texture: Brushed napped surface on the interior for insulation and soft hand-feel. Outer facing is smooth but slightly textured from the weave structure. Seams are visibly stitched with contrasting thread, emphasizing utilitarian construction.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal gray with minimal branding. Subtle tonal striping along the torso seams. Kangaroo pocket outlined in slightly lighter gray thread.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty full-length zipper with oversized pull tab, finished with rubberized grip material. Optional magnetic snap reinforcement at chest.
distinctive_features: Port-split hood design—right-side seam extends from shoulder to crown, creating open channel for neural clusters
Large kangaroo pocket with reinforced edges and interior depth for carrying small electronics or personal items
Double-stitched cuff reinforcement to prevent fraying after repeated wear
Brushed interior lining for thermal retention
Subtle Coldbreak Basics woven label at lower left hem, deliberately understated
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional wear. Affordable circuit market brand, not luxury, but intentional design rather than salvage. Signals working-class augmentation acceptance.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street culture, corpo mid-tier employees who keep augmentations visible, medical workers on off-hours, indie contractors. Wearing this says: 'I have port hardware and I'm not hiding it; I shop practical; I don't perform for corporate aesthetics.' Not salvage culture, not wealthy, just real.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn broken-in on first wear. After 3-6 months: subtle pilling on high-friction areas (lower hem, pocket edges), slight fading of charcoal, possible selective distressing from port contact wear. Still functional and acceptable for years. Rarely looks pristine.
